transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I came in because I've been having some issues at work. I'm a cashier, and lately... I just keep getting stuck doing things at the register that don't really fit the moment. 

Like, I'll start tapping the scanner in a certain pattern, or I'll just freeze completely with my hand hovering right over the cash drawer while the customer is standing there waiting on me. It's been happening a lot, and, well, last week it actually got me written up. So I figured I needed to come see someone about it.
Do you find yourself having repeated thoughts that you can't control, or do you feel like you have to perform certain actions in a specific way to reduce anxiety?

No, it's not really like that. I don't... I don't have thoughts telling me to do it or anything. And I wouldn't say I feel anxious before it happens, either. It's just... it just happens. I don't feel like I *have* to do it to fix something in my head, my body just starts doing it, or stops doing anything at all.
Do these actions happen without you being aware of them, or do you realize you're doing them while it's happening?

I... I usually realize it while it's happening. It's not like I black out or forget where I am. I'm just standing there, and I know I'm tapping the scanner or just frozen, but I can't really... snap out of it right away. I see the customer looking at me, I know they're waiting, but my body just stays stuck in whatever it's doing.
Before these episodes happen, do you ever feel a strange sensation or an urge in your body that makes you feel like something needs to be done or felt just right?

No, I don't feel anything like that. There's no... no build-up or urge in my body beforehand. I don't feel like things need to be just right, or anything like that. It just happens on its own, without any warning or feeling leading up to it.
Have you noticed these kinds of episodes happening anywhere other than work, like when you're at home or doing other activities?

No, not really. I... I haven't noticed it happening at home or anywhere else. It seems to mostly just be when I'm at work. When I'm at home, I'm usually just by myself, so... I don't think it happens there. At least, I haven't caught myself doing it.
Have you ever noticed any other times when your body moves on its own without you meaning to, like sudden jerks, twitches, or other movements, even if they're small?
No, I haven't noticed anything like that. No jerks or twitches... just the freezing up or the tapping at work. My body doesn't really move on its own otherwise.
Have you experienced or witnessed any traumatic or highly stressful events around the time these episodes at work started happening?

No, nothing like that. I mean... work can get a little busy sometimes, just being on the register, but I haven't been through anything traumatic. There hasn't been any major stress or big events lately. It's really just been the usual day-to-day routine.
Have you ever had episodes like this before, even if just once or twice, or is this something that's only started recently?

No, I don't think so. I haven't had anything like this happen before. It's... it's just been recently, over the last little while. Before this started at work, everything was pretty normal. So, no, nothing like this in the past.
While you're having one of these episodes at work, are you fully aware of what's going on around you, or do you feel spaced out or confused during it?

No, I'm fully aware. I... I hear the customers, I know I'm standing at the register. I don't feel confused or spaced out at all. I just get stuck, or I'm doing that tapping thing. But my mind is right there, I know exactly what's happening around me.
Have you ever had anything like these episodes happen to you before, even just once or twice, even if it didn't happen repeatedly like it is now?
No, like I mentioned just a minute ago, I really haven't. Not even once or twice. I've never dealt with anything like this in the past until this all started recently.
Has anyone in your family ever been diagnosed with a neurological condition or a movement disorder, like Parkinson’s disease, Huntington’s disease, or something similar?

No, not that I know of. Nobody in my family has ever had Parkinson's or Huntington's, or anything like that. As far as I know, there's no history of any neurological issues or movement problems with my parents or anyone else in the family.
Have you ever been diagnosed with any psychiatric or developmental conditions, like anxiety, depression, autism, or obsessive-compulsive disorder?
No, I haven't. I've never been diagnosed with anxiety or depression, or anything like OCD or autism. I've never really had any mental health issues or seen a psychiatrist before now.
While you're having one of these episodes, do you ever feel like you're losing control of yourself, or like part of you is watching what's happening without being able to take over?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I don't feel like I'm watching myself from the outside or anything like that. And I don't really feel like I'm losing control of my body... it's more just what I was saying before. But no, I haven't noticed feeling disconnected or like I can't take over.
Have you ever used any substances, like drugs or medications, that might affect the way your body moves or how your mind works?

No, I haven't. I don't use any drugs or anything like that. Just... maybe an aspirin if I have a headache, but that's it. I haven't taken any medications or substances that would mess with my mind or make my body move weirdly.
Have you ever noticed these episodes happening in response to specific triggers, like stress or being distracted, even if they haven’t occurred outside of work?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, I guess work can be a little stressful sometimes, just being a cashier and dealing with people all day, but... no, I haven't noticed any specific triggers. It just sort of happens when it happens. I haven't really connected it to being distracted or stressed out.

Have you noticed any very small or subtle movements that you don't mean to do, like slight eye blinking, lip movements, or fingers twitching slightly—even if it's not as noticeable as the freezing or tapping at work?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I don't have any weird blinking or lip movements. And my fingers... well, aside from the tapping I already told you about, they don't really twitch on their own or anything. So, no, I haven't seen any of those little movements.
Have you ever experienced any episodes where you temporarily couldn't move your body, especially when falling asleep or just waking up?
No, nothing like that. When I wake up or go to sleep, I can move just fine. I haven't ever been stuck or frozen in bed or anything. It's just normal sleep for me.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts aren't your own or that something outside of you is making your body move during these episodes?

No, I haven't felt anything like that. My thoughts are my own... and when my body moves, or when I do the tapping, it's just me doing it. I don't feel like something else is controlling me or putting thoughts in my head. It's just me.
Do you ever feel any unusual sensations in your body, like tingling, tightness, or something else, just before or during these episodes at work?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. There's no tingling or... or tightness or anything. My body just feels normal right before the tapping or the freezing happens. I don't get any weird physical sensations at all.

inference_history.note: The patient reports awareness during the episodes, ruling out disorders primarily characterized by loss of awareness or compulsive behaviors driven by anxiety (e.g., F32, F33, F94.8). The lack of intrusive thoughts or a sense of compulsion also makes F42 less likely but still possible. F20 and F21 remain plausible given the possible dissociative or motor disturbances. F06 is retained due to possible organic basis given the involuntary actions, but less specific at this point.

The patient reports that the episodes occur only at work and involve either freezing or repetitive tapping. These movements occur without preceding urges, anxiety, or a sense of being compelled to perform them, which makes OCD (F42) less likely. There is no evidence of involuntary movements outside of these specific episodes, reducing the likelihood of a primary movement disorder or schizophrenia spectrum disorder (F20, F21). The presentation does not clearly align with any of the current candidates, but further evaluation is needed. No new disorder is ruled in or out definitively.

The patient's symptoms do not appear to be driven by obsessive thoughts, compulsive behaviors, or anxiety, which makes OCD (F42) less likely. There is no history of trauma, which makes PTSD (F43.1) unlikely. The patient is aware during the episodes and does not display confusion or altered consciousness, which reduces the likelihood of organic causes such as seizures or delirium (F06). However, the involuntary motor behavior and lack of voluntary control could still be consistent with a schizophrenia spectrum disorder (F20), a delusional disorder (F22), or other non-affective psychotic disorder (F21). No new disorder has been ruled out definitively, but the lack of compulsions, trauma, or altered awareness has narrowed the focus.
